title: Tabulate the derived invariant beside the raw parameter
statement: Before searching, compute the invariant the theory says controls the phenomenon (discriminant, class number, modulus) and tabulate it beside the raw parameter. The answer is often invisible until the two columns sit together.

title: Reduce to a family with a provable bound so results are theorems
statement: Find a bound beyond which the object cannot occur, then enumerate exhaustively below it. Results become theorems rather than samples.

title: Group counts by a derived invariant, not the raw parameter
statement: When counts look noisy in the raw parameter, group by the invariant that the mechanism predicts (a gcd, a modulus, a residue class) and check whether the noise collapses.

title: Exploit state-space collapse: multiset or sorted form instead of integer
statement: If the map is invariant under a symmetry (digit permutation, reversal), enumerate orbits of the quotient rather than raw integers. Cycle structure becomes finite and checkable.

title: Reproduce a known value before trusting a method
statement: Run the method on an input with a published answer first. A method that cannot reproduce the known value produces nothing usable on the unknown one.

title: Check the argmax against the search ceiling
statement: A maximiser pressed against the search bound is not a record; it is the bound. Report the ceiling, extend it, and only then report a maximum.

title: Reduce a search to the image of the map
statement: Instead of searching inputs, characterise the image of the map and search there. Fixed points of a digit map are solutions of an equation over the image, which is far smaller.

title: Reduce a conjecture to a sharper sub-question and attack the intersection
statement: Find the conjunction of two known conditions a counterexample must satisfy and attack the intersection directly, rather than filtering one set by the other.

title: Look for a congruence obstruction when a size bound stops improving
statement: Reciprocal and size bounds saturate quickly. The next lever is a congruence the object must satisfy that no candidate can, found by computing the object modulo small primes.

title: Treat reverse-and-add as a finite carry transducer and eliminate radially
statement: Model each column as a bounded integer equation with carry variables, process opposite columns together from the outside in, and keep only the live interface. Bounded interface width makes exact elimination cheap and produces a replayable certificate.

title: Search for a minimal unsatisfiable core by exact countermodels
statement: Delete one constraint at a time, solve exactly, and keep the deletions that stay unsatisfiable. The surviving core is the obstruction; single-deletion satisfiability also proves it is the unique minimal one.

title: Perturb one interface of a fixed topology and re-solve
statement: Move exactly one block boundary by a bounded number of columns, regenerate the finite system, and solve each variant exactly. Classifies a neighbourhood of the topology as obstructed or not.

title: Test whether a construction lifts affinely to other bases
statement: Map each fixed digit d of a base-b construction to d or d plus the base difference, keep carries fresh, and solve the resulting system in the target base. Infeasibility at n=0 rules out the whole affine family.

title: Ask the LP relaxation for a Farkas certificate before trusting an integral obstruction
statement: Relax the integer system to an LP with elastic slacks. A zero-violation LP optimum proves no linear certificate exists and the obstruction is intrinsically integral, which tells a proof-format search which rules it must use.

title: Certify a small induced width per layer to explain why elimination is cheap
statement: Build the primal graph of each layer, derive an elimination order, and replay it to get a checkable upper bound on treewidth. Explains tractability without inferring it from solver behaviour.
